- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during prolonged downward trends; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion toward recent average.
- Overshoot after high peaks; cap forecast values at 10–15% below the peak to avoid overreaction.
- Lag in response to recent price drops; delay downward adjustments by 1–2 periods.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; smooth out extreme deviations using rolling 7-day average as a filter.
- Forecast bias toward higher values in early periods; apply downward correction for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5%, reduce next period’s forecast by 2–3% to avoid compounding overestimation.
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above the 30-day moving average unless accompanied by strong macro signals (e.g., policy changes, supply shocks).
